comments.author: architect-21d05545
comments.content:
PLAN-TIME REACHABILITY / SCOPE BLOCK (delivered-tree anchor HEAD b3a7551dfaaf9473a2bbabfb9cef93dda9b451ad). All seven existing owned paths were clean; the three declared new files are absent. Physical lines: contracts canonical 68, contracts index 228, daemon contracts 221, daemon protocol 305, live-handshake 307, use-goal-prd 108; no existing production source crosses 400. Both prerequisite rows are DONE/merged. `git grep` confirms generateSessionKey/openSessionRequestDigest/signSessionChallenge have no production Control Room caller; only producer barrel/tests/E2E use them. `apps/control-room/package.json` declares both @moe/control-room-client and @moe/contracts, pnpm-lock importer lines 74-79 link both workspaces, and a temporary `apps/control-room/src` compiled probe imported both bare specifiers under `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` exit 0, then was deleted by the same Node command.

The exact ten-path roster is insufficient for the required behavior and cannot be planned without violating rails 1/8. Changing resolveLiveSetupFromHandshake from bearer claim -> setup into key-bearing claim -> challenge -> signed `/session/pair/open` necessarily changes exact fetch/response expectations in at least THREE asserting consumers omitted from ownership: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-handshake.test.ts` (healthy path explicitly expects exactly bootstrap/request/claim and a claim body with no challenge), `apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-app.test.tsx` (real handshake fixtures return the old seven-key claim and no open route), and `tests/integration/control-room/pairing-claim-parity.test.ts` (drives daemon bearer/keyed claim bodies through the current client but serves no open route). Accepting those old keyed responses as a bearer fallback would contradict DoD 3's “no live setup until signed open succeeds” and fail open.

A second omitted production path is `packages/control-room-client/src/session-key.ts`: it owns `isKeyPair`, the 44-byte SPKI guard, and `SESSION_KEY_ALGORITHM_UNSUPPORTED@CONTROL_ROOM_SESSION_KEY`. DoD 4 and 5 require non-keypair/wrong-SPKI arms and a production mutation of that keypair guard; mutating or changing this unowned path is forbidden. `git grep` verified those guards are not present in any owned module.

Adding the four mandatory reachable paths to the ten listed paths yields 14 distinct files, beyond the daemon's <=10 plan cap, so this is a SPIDR split signal rather than an amendment. Suggested production slices: (A) shared browser-safe proof framing/constants with contracts+daemon compatibility; (B) real keyed live pairing with session-key.ts, live-keyed-session, live-handshake, and all three existing caller tests; (C) PRD pure-reader plus runtime-provider hostile table after A/B, retaining exact code/layer and denominator drills. The `moe-epic-breakdown` skill required before filing split rows is not installed/exposed in this session (only moe-planning/moe-qa-loop exist), so I did not invent child rows without it.
